body: Rodeo Drive - Special Events - Holiday Program Committee
name: Rodeo Drive / Special Events / Holiday Program Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Rodeo Drive Committee/Special
  Events/Holiday Program Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, May 22, 2024
  11:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  May 22, 2024 / 11:00 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells, Deputy City Manager
  Keith Sterling, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis, Public
  Works Associate Project Manager Teresa Revis Rodeo Drive Committee
  President Kay Monica Rose

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Review of Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Workplan and Funding request for the Rodeo Drive
  Committee (RDC), Including Website, Social Media, and “Rodeo Drive Celebrates”
  Program:
  a. The workplan does not cover the Concours d’Elegance or the Holiday Lighting
  Celebration Kick Off as these are covered in a separate partnership with a
  separate structure and separate agreements.
  b. The funding for the workplan and the events listed above comes from TOT
  revenue.
  c. The total funding request for the RDC 2024-2025 workplan is $197,998.
  d. The RDC’s social media pages have grown over the past year, with Instagram
  growing the largest.
  e. The RDC website has introduced a collections page, which spotlights the
  collections of RDC members, driving sales.
  f. Over the past year, the RDC has developed a new language plug in to assist
  international travelers.
  g. Their goal for the website this year is to perform SEO (Search Engine Optimization)
  to boost website traffic and to develop a dedicated celebrations page for Rodeo
  Drive Celebrates.
  h. The RDC social media pages have implemented a community engagement
  strategy which they attribute for their consistent growth over the past year. This
  has focused on actively engaging with the existing community while also sharing
  user generated content from influencers to attract followers.
  i. The total funding request for digital and website management for FY 2024-2025 is
  $184,998.
 Highlights for May 22, 2024
Rodeo Drive Committee/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  j. Both Mayor Friedman and Councilmember Wells are in favor of supporting the
  design of the August banners as well as the FY 2024-2025 budget.
  k. The Liaisons also recommended having the year over year budget from 2019 to
  now for BOLD when BOLD is presented to the council.

  3) Citywide Holiday Decor:
  a. Presentation by Teresa Revis:
  i. Following the direction from the January Liaison meeting, staff looked into
  replacing the décor on South Santa Monica, South Beverly, and La
  Cienega due to them nearing the end of their 5-year lifespan. They
  determined that the décor on South Santa Monica and La Cienega could
  be retained but that South Beverly needed to be replaced.
  ii. For South Beverly they decided to change out the twinkle lights on the tree
  trunks and make them colored lights. They also removed the multicolored
  sculptures due to them reaching the end of their service life.
  iii. They presented two options for the canopy decorations, either string
  mounted 9” plastic globes with warm white fairy lights or individually
  mounted warm white starlight spheres.
  iv. The up-front cost for either of the canopy lights would be $250,000 with the
  ongoing costs of instillation, removal, and storage being $128,000.
  v. The estimated lifespan of these lights would be around 5 years.
  vi. The cost estimate to refurbish the Wilshire Span lights was $351,000,
  which staff determined to be prohibitively high, so they are looking into
  other bids as well as doing an in depth look at what needs to be replaced
  and what can last for an additional year or two.
  vii. For the projection mapping, they are planning on upgrading the power at
  City Hall lawn with the goal of not using generators for the show this year.
  This would make the show both more reliable and more environmentally
  friendly.
  viii. The city is also working with the projection mapping’s primary contractor
  Utopia to find a new designer for the show this year.
  ix. For the Beverly Canon Gardens grass area there are 5 options, 3 from the
  city and 2 from the Maybourne. The 3 city options incorporate the same
  base tree from last year with a different décor package. The first is a
  Topiary Scroll design, the second is a Gold Pine Cone, and the third is a
  Cool White Star with 4 alternatives. The two Maybourne options are a Red
  option with options for lights and a White option with options for lights.
  x. The holiday lighting kickoff event this year will be on November 14th.
  b. If the Maybourne options have an additional cost the Maybourne will participate in
  that additional cost.
  c. Both Liaisons expressed a preference for the Maybourne’s white option for Beverly
  Canon Gardens.
  d. The Projection Mapping has an annual cost of $750,000 with the largest expense
  being the equipment rentals.
  e. Once all the content is designed, they would reduce the annual Projection mapping
  costs by around $100,000.
 Highlights for May 22, 2024
Rodeo Drive Committee/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  f. Councilmember Wells expressed skepticism about continuing the Projection
  Mapping due to it both being out of the way and its operating costs.
  g. For the lawn electrical upgrade, the mayor is interested in establishing a fee
  structure for others who will use the upgrade in place of generators.

  4) Future Agenda Items:
  a. None

  5) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: May 10, 2024 / 12:34 PM
